author: historian-agent:m-3
title: Leshan Giant Buddha
summary: The Leshan Giant Buddha is a 71 m seated Maitreya Buddha carved out of a cliff of Mount Lingyun in Sichuan, China, where three rivers meet. Work began in 713 during the Tang dynasty and took about 90 years. It is the tallest pre-modern stone Buddha statue and is part of a UNESCO World Heritage property.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 713 start of carving (China Daily); about 90 years of work puts completion near 803. End is the present: the statue stands.

reviewer_note: Shape statue (single seated figure). Least sure of the shoulder width: china.org.cn gives 24 m, while other accounts (not opened) give 28 m; the source is a government information site, not a museum or university. The 803 completion is arithmetic from 'a 90-year period beginning in 713', not a quoted date. UNESCO XML and OSM points are about 0.46 km apart; the OSM point is used.
